stem: Which districts in Bihar will benefit from the Kosi Mechi Link Project?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The Kosi–Mechi Link Project is an intra-state river-linking project within Bihar. Under this project, the Eastern Kosi Main Canal will be redeveloped and extended up to the Mechi River. This will provide irrigation facilities in about 2,10,516 hectares of additional area during the Kharif season. The main beneficiary districts will be Araria, Purnia, Kishanganj, and Katihar.

stem: In which agro-climatic region of Bihar are the maximum number of districts located?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Bihar falls in Agro-Climatic Region IV, known as the Middle Gangetic Plains Region. On the basis of soil characteristics, rainfall, temperature, and physiography, Bihar is divided into three sub-regions: North-East alluvial plains, North-West alluvial plains, and South Bihar alluvial plains. The South Bihar alluvial plains are further classified into South-East (A) and South-West (B). The North-West zone includes a total of 12 districts, while the North-East zone includes 8 districts. The South Bihar alluvial plains zone has 17 districts, out of which 6 are in the South-East zone (A) and 11 are in the South-West zone (B). Thus, it is clear that the maximum number of districts are included in the North-West zone.

stem: What is the percentage of population employed in agriculture in the state of Bihar in 2017-18?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2018–19, about 74 percent of the state’s workforce was employed in agriculture, which was much higher than the national average. According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, more than 75 percent of the workforce of the state was engaged in agricultural activities.

stem: In which district of Bihar, Litchi production is maximum ?
expl: According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2023–24, in the year 2022–23 the highest litchi production in Bihar was recorded in Muzaffarpur (147.95 thousand tonnes). Litchi production in Siwan was 8.70 thousand tonnes. Sonpur and Chhapra are not districts of Bihar; Chhapra is the headquarters of Saran district. According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, in the year 2023–24 also the highest litchi production was recorded in Muzaffarpur (101.52 thousand tonnes)

stem: The average size of landholdings in Bihar in comparison with other states is –

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the Agricultural Census 2015–16, the average size of landholding in Bihar is 0.39 hectare. The average landholding size is smaller in Daman and Diu (0.36 hectare), Kerala (0.18 hectare), and Lakshadweep (0.27 hectare). From the viewpoint of states, Bihar ranks second lowest in terms of average size of landholdings.

stem: What percent of cultivable land in Bihar is irrigated?
expl: At the time of the examination, option (a) was the correct answer. According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, in the year 2022–23 the gross sown area in Bihar was 7268.2 thousand hectares, out of which the gross irrigated area was 5697.9 thousand hectares, which constituted 78.39 percent of the total gross sown area.

stem: The percentage of net cultivated area out of total area in Bihar is –
expl: At the time of the examination, option (a) was the correct answer. According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, in the year 2022–23 the total net sown area was 5112.8 thousand hectares, which constituted about 54.63 percent of Bihar’s total geographical area of 9359.6 thousand hectares.

stem: In which district of Bihar, maize production is maximum ?
expl: According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2023–24, among the given options, in the year 2022–23 maize production was highest in Muzaffarpur (156.36 thousand tonnes), followed by East Champaran (135.39 thousand tonnes), Siwan (57.37 thousand tonnes), and Saran (78.67 thousand tonnes). However, the highest maize production overall was recorded in Araria (987.26 thousand tonnes). According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2024–25, in the year 2023–24 the highest maize production was recorded in Purnia (1144.9 thousand tonnes), followed by Araria (829.8 thousand tonnes) and Katihar (622.8 thousand tonnes).

stem: In which district of Bihar, wheat crop production is maximum ?
expl: According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2023–24, in the year 2022–23 the highest production of wheat was in Rohtas district (675.88 thousand tonnes). Wheat production in Jehanabad was 69.02 thousand tonnes, in Bhojpur 356.24 thousand tonnes, and in Patna 245.63 thousand tonnes. According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, in the year 2023–24 the highest wheat production was in Rohtas district (716.2 thousand tonnes). Thereafter, Muzaffarpur (400.1 thousand tonnes) and Bhojpur (386.8 thousand tonnes).

stem: The leading sugarcane producer district of Bihar is –

options.label: e

expl: At the time of the question as well as at present, option (a) is the correct answer. According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, in the year 2023–24 the highest sugarcane production was in West Champaran (9,667,743 metric tonnes). Thereafter, East Champaran (1,325,554 metric tonnes), Gopalganj (697,653 metric tonnes), and Sitamarhi (637,287 metric tonnes) were next.

stem: Leading fish producer districts of Bihar are:

In the year 2017–18, the total production of coarse cereals was 3.15 lakh tonnes. Between 2013–14 and 2017–18, a growth rate of 6 percent was recorded.

stem: In which district of Bihar is the highest production of Makhana?
expl: Among the given options, Madhubani district has the highest production of makhana in Bihar. Darbhanga, Purnia, Saharsa, Katihar, Supaul, Madhepura, Araria, and Kishanganj are other major makhana-producing districts.

stem: The district with the highest jute production in Bihar is -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Among the options given above, the highest production of jute in Bihar is in Purnia district. According to the Directorate of Jute Development, in 2023–24, the highest jute production in India was in the state of West Bengal. West Bengal accounts for 81.15% of total jute production, Assam 6.95%, and Bihar 10.17%. As per the data for 2023–24, the top four jute-producing districts of Bihar are, respectively—Katihar (41,945 metric tons), Kishanganj (41,237 metric tons), Araria (25,851 metric tons), and Madhepura (18,393 metric tons)

stem: In terms of production in Bihar, the second crop after rice is -
expl: At the time of the question, in undivided Bihar (including Jharkhand), rice had the highest production. Thereafter, wheat production was next. expl: In Bihar, tea gardens were established for the first time at Thakurganj (Kishanganj). It is noteworthy that tea is cultivated on about 25 thousand acres of land in Bihar. However, Kishanganj district is the principal place for tea cultivation in Bihar.

stem: The largest canal irrigated area of Bihar lies in the district of –

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In Bihar, in the matter of irrigation through canals, in 2020–21 Rohtas district ranked first with 3.07 lakh hectares; thereafter West Champaran (1.85 lakh hectares) and Aurangabad (1.61 lakh hectares) were next. In gross irrigated area also, Rohtas district ranked first with 4.15 lakh hectares. According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, in 2022–23 the highest gross irrigated area through canals was in Rohtas district (299.40 thousand hectares). stem: Which one of the following cereals has the highest per hectare yield in Bihar?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to data for the year 2018-19, the productivity (kg/ ha) of crops in Bihar was: Rice – 1948, Wheat – 2998, Maize – 4771 and Barley – 1990. Bihar Economic Survey, 2020-21 in the year 2019-20, productivity was: Rice – 2245 kg/ha, Wheat – 2595 kg/ha, Maize – 5193 kg/ha and Barley – 1369 kg/ha. Thus, maize recorded the highest productivity in both years. Bihar Economic Survey 2024-25 in the year 2023-24, productivity was: Rice – 3062 kg/ha, Wheat – 3211 kg/ha, Maize – 6138 kg/ha and Barley – 1641 kg/ha.

stem: Which is the main cash crop of the state of Bihar?
expl: The major cash crops of Bihar are sugarcane, tobacco, jute and mesta. Among these, sugarcane occupies the first position in terms of both value and production.

stem: The top ranking pulses in terms of acreage in Bihar are –

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2019-20, in 2018-19, the production of Bhadai Moong was 5.32 thousand tons and that of Garma Moong was 113.16 thousand tons. Thus, the total Moong production was 118.48 thousand tons. During the same period, the production of lentils was 148.03 thousand tons, gram was 67.69 thousand tons, and Khesari was 51.38 thousand tons. stem: Which one of the following statements about irrigation in Bihar is not correct?

options.label: a
options.text: Of the total sown area in Bihar nearly 30 percent is irrigated.

options.label: b
options.text: Of the total irrigated area in Bihar nearly 30 percent is irrigated by canals and 39 percent by tubewells.

options.label: c
options.text: The maximum area irrigated by canals is found in Bhojpur, Aurangabad, West Champaran, Rohtas and Munger districts.

options.label: d
options.text: The maximum area irrigated by tube wells is found in Samastipur, Sitamarhi, Begusarai, Sitamarhi, Begusarai, Muzaffarpur, Gopalganj and Khagaria districts.

expl: At the time of the question, option (b) was the correct answer. According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, in the year 2022–23, 78.39 percent of the gross cropped area of Bihar was irrigated. Of the total irrigated area of Bihar (5,697.9 thousand hectares), 30.28 percent area was irrigated by canals and 63.41 percent area by tube wells. The districts having the highest gross irrigated area through canals, respectively, are Rohtas, West Champaran, Bhojpur, Aurangabad and Kaimur. Whereas the districts having the highest gross irrigated area through tube wells, respectively, are Samastipur, Sitamarhi, Nalanda, Muzaffarpur and East Champaran.

stem: Joint irrigation project of the States of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh is –

This project is constructed on the Gandak River near Valmiki Nagar in Bihar. Two canals have been taken out from it— (1) Tirhut Main Canal (2) Saran Main Canal

stem: Finally, what is the irrigation capacity of Bihar?
expl: At the time of the question, option (a) was correct. According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, in the year 2023–24, the utilized irrigation potential of major and medium irrigation projects in Bihar was 26.7 lakh hectares, while the created irrigation potential was 37.72 lakh hectares. In the case of minor irrigation, the utilized potential was 43.31 lakh hectares, whereas the created potential was 48.12 lakh hectares.

stem: The traditional water conservation irrigation method prevalent in South Bihar is called -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The traditional water conservation irrigation system prevalent in South Bihar is called Ahar–Pyne. In this system, retention ponds and channels or canals are used for the management of water resources.

stem: After independence the irrigated area in Bihar enlarged approximately-
expl: After independence, the irrigated area in Bihar has increased by approximately ten times. At present (2023–24), the created irrigation potential in Bihar is 85.84 lakh hectares.

stem: What type of banks are proposed to be set up in Bihar for agriculture and rural development?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In October, 2021, during the 'Rabi Mahabhiyan' launched by the Chief Minister of Bihar, Nitish Kumar, it was announced to establish Krishi Yantra Bank for providing farmers with necessary agricultural implements for modern farming.
